players.outlook: Christian Watson will look to build off a career day as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Watson put together a prolific performance in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, bringing in seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown. The wideout now holds a career-high receiving line of 49-879-7 on 74 targets. He'll face a Minnesota secondary that he tore up with 6 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns against in Week 1.

Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in Week 10 as the Packers take on the Vikings. Jacobs hurt his finger in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, and he's now set to undergo surgery, which will keep him out for a maximum of three weeks. The veteran ball carrier has now recorded 36 rushes for 80 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches for 68 yards and two touchdowns as well. Kaleb Johnson, Pierre Strong, and banged-up Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd will be Green Bay's available running backs against a tough Minnesota defense.

news.text: Jacobs (finger) has a "realistic chance" of returning to action Nov. 25 against the Rams following the Packers' Week 11 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.. Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. He has 14 targets over the last two weeks as Malik Washington's role shrinks, and Douglas has 70 receiving yards in two of his last three outings despite Malik Willis' struggles. news.text: Douglas (shoulder) remained a limited practice participant Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.. The listing makes sense, given that Douglas, who was also deemed limited Wednesday, worked in a  non-contact jersey Thursday. Fellow WR Chris Bell (knee) has also logged back-to-back 'LP' listings, with the duo's game statuses for Sunday's game against the Bills set to be revealed after Friday's practice session.

players.outlook: Puka Nacua is expected to miss the Rams' Week 10 clash against the Cardinals and several weeks beyond that. Nacua suffered a knee injury in this past Sunday's win over Washington and is likely to be placed on IR. Davante Adams (hamstring) remains on IR, so the Rams' WR corps will be led by the likes of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington.

news.text: Nacua has been suspended three games for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.. Nacua currently resides on injured reserve due to PCL and MCL sprains and a turf toe injury, for which he still must miss at least three games. The announced suspension conveniently lines up with his remaining expected time away from the field, and he'll be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14, following the completion of the the Rams' Week 14 contest versus the 49ers. players.outlook: Brock Bowers was nearly the only Raider to find any success in a Week 9 loss to the 49ers, turning eight targets into seven catches for 111 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has scored six times in seven games since making a belated season debut, and Bowers delivered a 48-658-6 line on 70 targets as Kirk Cousins' clear No. 1 downfield option. He's now likely Francisco Mendoza's top option and will look to keep rolling in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

news.text: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.. Bowers missed Wednesday's practice, but his return a day later, albeit in a limited fashion, is a positive sign as Sunday's game against the Broncos approaches. Head coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that the star tight end didn't need to practice this week in order to play this weekend, per Sam Warren of The Athletic, but Bowers has already cleared his first hurdle toward that end by virtue of his participation in Thursday's session.

players.outlook: Trey McBride could be extremely busy for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams. McBride has already been drawing constant attention in the Arizona passing game, recording at least seven catches and eight targets in all nine of the team's games this year. Now that top wideouts Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are likely done for the season, McBride may be even more heavily targeted. However, he'll be working with rookie QB Carson Beck for the first time due to Gardner Minshew's potentially season-ending elbow injury. McBride will also be going up against a Rams defense that

He finished with just two grabs for the contest, though did gain 53 yards total on the receptions. While Pickens may be shelved for Week 10 as well, Flournoy will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. He has rushed for over 100 yards in three of his last four games, averaging a whopping 121.8 rushing yards per game during that span. He now ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing yards per game (91.0) while scoring six total touchdowns in eight appearances this season. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is expected to continue leaning on the run game, which has led the Buccaneers to a 3-1 record over the last four weeks-a positive sign for Irving's outlook. Mike Evans continues to tend to an Achilles injury and is iffy to suit up for San Francisco in Week 10 against Dallas. The injury has prevented Evans from playing in each of the 49ers' past two games despite the team's bye being sandwiched between those contests. Fellow starting wideout Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has also been out, but the 49ers did add depth at the trade deadline by bringing in Keenan Allen. If Evans can return in Week 10, he'll square off against a Cowboys defense that ranks a poor 25th in the league with 23.4 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.

news.text: Evans (Achilles) officially was limited at Thursday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.. Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

players.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals welcome the divisional-rival Steelers to town for a Week 10 meeting on Sunday Night Football. He stayed red-hot in Week 9, completing 24 of 29 pass attempts for 271 yards and three TDs with no INTs, while rushing three times for seven yards and another score. Burrow owns a 16:3 TD:INT ratio and has two rushing TDs over his last four outings, and he continues to lead the NFL with 23 passing TDs through eight games. Jonah Coleman may be emerging as the Broncos' lead running back. The 2026 fourth-round pick topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time in a comeback win over Kansas City in Week 8, and he scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run after getting Denver into the red zone with a 51-yard catch-and-run. J.K. Dobbins logged seven carries, compared to Coleman's 15 total touches, and with RJ Harvey on injured reserve, the path is clear for the rookie to handle a significant workload. Dak Prescott posted his third 300-yard passing outing of the season for Dallas in Week 9, throwing for 335 yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Colts. He's thrown for multiple touchdowns in two of the last three contests. However, in Week 10, Prescott will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Francisco has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.

Jahmyr Gibbs will seek to return to dominance as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Gibbs punched in another rushing score alongside 74 yards on the ground in Week 9 against the Dolphins, but he was unable to record a catch for the first time this season. The star ball carrier has now recorded 20 or more carries in each of his last four outings, but he's seen his receiving work decline each week in that stretch. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

Denzel Boston and the Browns welcome the 3-5 Texans to town in Week 10. He corralled six of seven targets for 98 yards during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. Boston just missed the 100-yard mark but established a new career high in receiving yards, pacing his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He showed great rapport with Shedeur Sanders, who earned his first start of the season, but Deshaun Watson (concussion) is likely to return from a one-game absence to face his former team. Blake Corum continues to get a hefty share of work out of the Rams' backfield heading into a Week 10 visit to Arizona. Corum led Los Angeles with 58 rushing yards and scored a touchdown on 11 carries in a Week 9 win against Washington. Though he remains marginally behind Kyren Williams in the Rams' backfield, Corum has logged double-digit carries in three straight games and has scored in each of those contests. There could be an opportunity for both Corum and Williams to succeed against a Cardinals defense that is giving up 99.6 rushing yards per game to RBs, ranking 19th in the league.

They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the receiver's former team when the Colts come to town in Week 5. He hauled in two of four targets for 15 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, giving him a 7-89-0 receiving line on 12 targets across three contests. It's been a slow start for Pittman in his debut season for the Steelers, but Week 5 offers a shot at some payback against the team that drafted him in 2020. Indianapolis' defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs, a matchup that could help Pittman's chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.

news.text: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.. After he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman practiced for the second day in a row. Pittman took a step forward in activity after he was a limited participant a day earlier, potentially putting him on a path to return from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Philadelphia. In order for Pittman to be eligible to play against the Eagles, the Steelers would have to activate him prior to Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline for Week 11 roster moves.

players.outlook: CeeDee Lamb took advantage of the absence of George Pickens last game for Dallas. While Lamb is always the top target in the offense, with Pickens out of the lineup Lamb was targeted even more frequently than usual, a total of 16 times against the Colts. Lamb responded with 10 catches for a staggering 195 yards and a touchdown. Lamb has double-digit targets in four-straight games, and Pickens remains questionable for the Week 10 clash with the 49ers. Javonte Williams got back into the end zone last game for Dallas. Williams scored his ninth rushing touchdown of the season in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Williams also crossed the 100-yard rushing plateau for the second time in 2026. Williams has at least 20 carries in each of the last three outings. However, in Week 10, he will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 80.9 rushing yards per game, which is second in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for second in the NFL.

Jayden Daniels threw for 274 yards and a touchdown last game for Washington. He has passed for at least one touchdown in three-straight outings, and thrown for at least 270 yards in two of those three contests. In Week 10, he will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league, and Daniels ran for 103 yards and two scores when the two teams met earlier this season.

Lamar Jackson is heading to the IR after taking just one snap for the Ravens in Week 9. He missed the prior three contests with a high-ankle injury, and now thumb surgery could end his season. Tyler Huntley took over, but he had to exit with a toe injury, forcing emergency third-string QB Joe Fagnano into action. More will be known about Jackson's status after he goes under a very small knife.

news.text: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.. Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. players.outlook: Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs where he'll be catching passes from Patrick Mahomes, assuming the QB is healthy after hurting his elbow in Week 9. Downs will enjoy a QB upgrade, but he'll face more competition for targets from Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. With Worthy also nursing an injury, Downs could log a big workload in Week 10 against a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Jason Myers will hope for more kicking opportunities when Seattle faces Las Vegas in Week 10. Myers made his lone field goal and both his extra-point tries in Week 9 against Arizona as the Seahawks scored fewer than 21 points for the fourth straight week. The veteran kicker has been good when called upon this season, though, making 16 of 18 FG tries through nine games. He could be more active against the Raiders, who are giving up a league-worst 29.8 points per game.

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

Bhayshul Tuten played through foot and ankle injuries in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens. He scored his fifth touchdown in the past three games but was held to a season-low 29 scrimmage yards, less than half of his previous low of 62 yards from Week 2. Tuten has had a few extra days to recover since last Thursday's win and should be ready to assume his usual role as Jacksonville's top RB for a juicy Week 10 road matchup against the Titans, who are allowing 135 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. He profiles as a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 in fantasy for Week 10, especially if his pract

news.text: Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.. Tuten was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, so his downgrade in activity a day later is notable, though the listing could be maintenance-related rather than due to a setback.  O'Halloran previously relayed that the running back was working off to the side during the media-access portion of Thursday's session. The extent of Tuten's participation in Friday's practice bears watching, as the Jaguars look to determine whether he'll take an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Giants.

players.outlook: Omar Cooper will seek a consistent role when the Jets face the Bills in Week 10. Over the last four games, Cooper topped 100 yards twice, collecting double-digit targets in Week 9 after being shut out in Week 8. The additional looks came with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined, and while Wilson likely returns for Week 10, the Jets also figure to need to pass often to keep up with Buffalo's potent offense. Cooper will come with a high ceiling and ample volatility against a secondary that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points to wideouts but a mere 7.5 yards per target.

news.text: Cooper didn't practice Thursday due to ankle and hip injuries.. Cooper made an early exit from this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle, and the rookie wideout is also nursing a hip issue as the Jets prepare for a matchup this weekend with the Chargers. With two straight absences from practice to begin the week, Cooper will likely need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance at suiting up Sunday.

players.outlook: The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. Jordan Mason will look to see a more favorable game script in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Mason rushed just six times for 35 yards and reeled in two of three targets for seven yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. As expected, the fifth-year ball carrier has been a part of a two-pronged backfield approach next to Aaron Jones this season, but it appears Mason might be the more efficient of the pair. The Packers have ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

Brandon Aubrey missed yet another long field goal last game for Dallas. Aubrey did make two other tries, though pulled a 50-yarder wide left in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Aubrey is now 3-for-8 on attempts from 50-plus yards out this season. In Week 10, the Cowboys will face the 49ers. Points may be hard to come by, as San Fran is allowing just 19.5 points per tilt, which is sixth in the league.

Chris Rodriguez has scored in four of Jacksonville's last six games, but he hasn't topped 58 scrimmage yards in a game all season and is averaging 33 yards per game as Bhayshul Tuten's backup heading into a Week 10 road game against the Titans. Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent Week 10 flex option against a Tennessee defense that has allowed plenty of yards to RBs but limited the position to six TDs in eight games. news.text: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.. Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited participation Wednesday to no activity during Thursday's practice.

players.outlook: Braelon Allen has reverted to a secondary option for the Jets with Breece Hall healthy ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Bills. Allen recorded just 10 touches in Hall's return in Week 9 after 19 or more opportunities over the last five weeks. With Hall a preferred option in the passing game and facing a defense that allows just 3.8 yards per carry, Allen is unlikely to collect enough usage to be in the Week 10 fantasy mix.

DJ Moore will look for increased volume when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. Moore collected only five targets in Week 9, his lowest total in any healthy outing of 2026, in a game where Josh Allen had minimal time to throw. While he'll likely have more time Sunday and Moore has remained the preferred option on drop-backs, the Jets have allowed only nine touchdown receptions to wideouts, seemingly capping Moore's potential.

Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top pass catcher during the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. London has cooled down after a terrific stretch of games from Weeks 3 through 5, averaging just 4.3 receptions and 52.8 receiving yards per game over Atlanta's last four contests. He's also averaging just 7.6 targets per game this season, his lowest mark since 2023, so it appears the Falcons are struggling to get him involved. The star running back is second in the NFL in rushing yards with 872, just behind Bijan Robinson's 880. He is fourth in scrimmage yards with 1,044, and tied for first with Jahmyr Gibbs in total TDs from scrimmage with 11. news.text: Walker (groin) did not practice Thursday.. Walker is looking extremely unlikely to play Sunday against a Cardinals team that Kansas City should handle with ease at home. The Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround against the Bills on Thanksgiving, and it may make sense to let Walker rest for another week in preparation for that contest, especially after rookie Emmett Johnson showed in Week 10 against Atlanta that he's more than capable of carrying the torch in the backfield. Fantasy players need to be prepared to be without Walker for at least one more week.

players.outlook: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Kraft didn't get to join in on any of the fun of Green Bay's offensive explosion in Week 9 over the Patriots, as he brought in just one of his three targets for one yard and rushed the ball twice for eight yards. He's now posted a 36-351-3 receiving line across the first nine games of the campaign. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he logged three catches for 65 yards against in Week 1.

DeVonta Smith missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky hamstring. Smith has played in just four contests in 2026 in what has been a lost season overall for 2-6 Philadelphia. If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.

Woody Marks has recorded between 17 and 20 touches for 74-85 yards in each of Houston's last four games, working in a bell-cow role in the absence of David Montgomery (groin). Montgomery looks likely to remain sidelined in Week 10 at Cleveland, which should keep Marks in the fantasy RB2 range thanks to his high touch floor against a Browns defense that's allowing 115 rushing yards per game to running backs. Marks hasn't scored since Week 4, while Cleveland has given up seven TDs to RBs in nine games.

news.text: Marks (concussion) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Colts.. After sustaining a concussion in this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns, Marks will be sidelined for the first time this season after he was unable to practice in any capacity on a short week. The second-year player had been operating as the Texans' clear lead back over the past four contests, but for at least one week, those duties are expected to fall to David Montgomery (groin), who has been cleared to return to action following a four-game absence. Once Marks clears the protocol, he could be form a timeshare with Montgomery.

players.outlook: Omarion Hampton turned 13 carries into a team-high 60 rushing yards in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, his second-highest total of the season. Keaton Mitchell handled 10 touches, and Kimani Vidal got eight, as offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel continues to deploy a backfield committee that limits the ceiling of all three players. Hampton appears to be first among equals for now, but the struggles of the entire offense present an extra obstacle for him to overcome. He'll try to build on last week's modest numbers in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points

Emeka Egbuka (foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has been sidelined for two consecutive games due to a concussion and a foot injury. During that span, the Buccaneers completed just seven of 14 pass attempts for 64 yards and one touchdown, proving Egbuka's importance to the passing game. He's expected to lead the team's WR room against a tough Bears secondary that's allowed just 29.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through seven games this season.

Corey Kiner could be in line for a significant role for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions, with both Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) uncertain to play. While Detroit is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing backs, volume remains king, and Kiner could serve as the No. 1 RB for Week 10 in Munich. Kiner figures to be a popular play in what could be a high-scoring game, despite Detroit allowing just 3.9 yards per carry.

Brock Purdy will continue to push toward MVP consideration when the 49ers face Dallas in Week 10. Purdy helped San Francisco improve to 7-1 this past Sunday with a win over the Raiders during which he threw for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception despite working without the team's top two wideouts, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Purdy also ran for 40 yards and a score in the victory, and he currently ranks sixth among NFL quarterbacks with 201 rushing yards on the campaign. Trey Smack will aim to stay on track as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. After a less-than-optimal start to the season, Smack reeled it in against the Patriots in Week 9, nailing all three field-goal attempts and four PATs. The rookie kicker has still made just five of his last nine field-goal tries, so he'll need to stay accurate against a Minnesota defense that he made three field goals against in Week 1.

Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. LaPorta was quiet again in Week 9 versus the Dolphins, amid a struggling Detroit passing offense, recording four catches for 32 yards. The starting tight end has totaled just 83 receiving yards in his last three games after going back-to-back weeks with 80-plus receiving yards and a touchdown heading into the Lions' bye. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

Zach Charbonnet seems to be emerging as Seattle's No. 1 running back heading into a Week 10 tilt against the Raiders. In his second game back from ACL surgery, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 16 carries and 77 receiving yards against Arizona this past Sunday while adding one catch for nine yards. Rookie Jadarian Price still managed 13 touches, so Charbonnet doesn't seem likely to have the backfield all to himself. Both tailbacks could thrive against a Las Vegas defense that has allowed a league-worst 5.21 yards per carry to running backs.

Eddy Pineiro hasn't had many chances for field goals of late ahead of San Francisco's Week 10 matchup against Dallas. Pineiro make his only FG attempt this past Sunday against the Raiders and has now attempted one or zero field goals in five of eight games this season. That's largely because the 49ers' offense has been so effective -- they have 22 TDs and just four FGs in 26 trips to the red zone. It could be more of the same for Pineiro against the Cowboys, who have allowed 27 PAT tries and 17 FG attempts this season.

Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top receiving options in the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Coker has cooled down along with the majority of Carolina's offense over the last three weeks, catching just seven of 14 targets for 74 yards and a touchdown during that span. Despite this, Bryce Young is still tied for the most pass attempts per game in the NFL (38.5), which bodes well for Coker's fantasy outlook going forward. Coker could take advantage of a New Orleans secondary that's given up 11.1 yards per completion this year.

Jameson Williams will look to get more volume as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Williams struggled to get touches with a stagnant passing game against the Dolphins in Week 9, recording one catch for 31 yards and one rush for nine yards. The speedy wideout has now posted a 28-468-5 receiving line on 44 targets across eight games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

Rachaad White continues to operate as the top back for the Commanders, though has found little room to roam on the ground. White has failed to rush for more than 55 yards in any game this season. However, he does have at least two receptions in three-straight contests. In Week 10, White will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league.

Courtland Sutton set new season highs in catches and receiving yards during the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but he still came away with just a 4-53-0 line on four targets. The struggles of quarterback Bo Nix, as well as the offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle, have reduced Sutton's target volume considerably from 2025, and he's on pace for only 79 targets this season after topping 120 in each of the prior two years. Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills offense may be sliding as they enter a Week 10 matchup against the Jets. In Buffalo's first six games, Kincaid garnered less than a 66% snap share just once, but since the team's Week 7 bye, he's been under 60% in two outings, resulting in just nine targets. The Jets have been vulnerable against tight ends, allowing at least 72 yards in three straight weeks, but Kincaid's recent workload is a concern.

news.text: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) wasn't spotted on the field for Thursday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.. Kincaid has now kicked off Week 11 prep with consecutive absences from practice, but he'll be able to erase some concern about his status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins if he's able to get back on the field Friday in some capacity.

players.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a rare quiet game with Seattle's Week 10 matchup in Las Vegas on tap. The All-Pro wideout logged a season-low 51 yards on seven catches this past Sunday against Arizona, though he still drew a healthy 10 targets. Drew Lock (oblique) started at quarterback for the Seahawks in that contest and is expected to do so again in Week 10, as Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib) is likely to remain sidelined. Regardless, Smith-Njigba could feast against a Raiders defense that ranks 26th in the league with 23.6 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT

Drake Maye appears poised for a busy outing in Week 10 when the Patriots face the Lions. Maye has tossed multiple touchdown passes in six straight outings (17 total), three times going for 299 yards or more, and could be asked to throw at a high rate with running backs TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson uncertain to suit up. Pair that with a matchup against a Lions secondary that's allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks, and Maye could provide elite numbers in Week 10's Sunday morning affair in Germany.

news.text: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't have a definitive diagnosis for the injury Maye (ankle) sustained in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but indicated that the quarterback will miss time," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.  "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said.. Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

Singletary had a season-high 21 carries due to the injury to Cam Skattebo, though managed just 31 yards in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. players.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Chargers to town for a Week 10 clash on Monday Night Football. He rushed 17 times for 57 yards and did not record a target during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. Henry has struggled mightily over his last four outings, gaining 213 yards on 62 carries (3.4 yards per carry) with just one touchdown. Jacoby Brissett, who's expected to start under center in Week 10, should provide some relief for the passing game, so the hope is that this will begin to have a positive effect on Henry.

Breece Hall's workload should be strong in the Jets' Week 10 matchup against a tough Bills run defense. Returning to action in Week 9 after a five-game absence, Hall collected 18 touches to Braelon Allen's 10, despite Allen's success while Hall was sidelined. Hall has logged at least 13 carries in all four games when healthy, adding 13 receptions. His viability in the passing game should allow him to be a fantasy factor despite facing a defense that's allowing just 3.8 yards per carry.

Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Kamara received fewer than 10 touches for the third time in New Orleans' last four games during the Week 9 win over the Browns, despite backfield mate Kendre Miller being release prior to the contest. Regardless, Kamara ranks first amongst Saints RBs in targets (31), receptions (25), receiving yards (150) and receiving touchdowns (one) in seven appearances this year. Travis Kelce produced his highest yardage total since Week 2 in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, hauling in four of six targets for a team-high 72 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2021 on a one-yard plunge. Kelce has delivered a 33-482-2 line on 48 targets through eight games, but his outlook would suffer if Patrick Mahomes ends up missing time due to an elbow injury he picked up against the Jets. Regardless of who's under center, Kelce will face a Falcons defense in Week 10 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made and attempted, even with his volume and effectiveness dropping off in recent weeks as the 2-7 Colts continue to struggle as a team. He's 22-for-24 this season but just 4-for-6 over the past three games. Indianapolis faces a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed 15 made field goals in eight games and 25.0 points per game. If you have Shrader on your roster, you may as well keep starting him.

Aaron Jones will look to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Packers in Week 10. Jones saw just five carries and one target in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, and he took them for 16 yards and five yards, respectively. The veteran running back has now seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, logging 18 carries in total during that stretch. He's not likely to see crazy value with Jordan Mason active, but a Green Bay defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.

Matthew Golden will look to keep his tear rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Golden logged a career-best 164 yards on 10 catches and found the end zone in a Week 9 win over the Patriots. The second-year breakout receiver also caught every one of his targets in the win, which was a huge improvement from some drop-heavy games this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he caught six passes for 95 yards against in Week 1.

Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will look to return from a four-game absence when San Francisco travels to Dallas in Week 10. Samuel hasn't been placed on IR, and the expectation is that he'll return before the end of the season, but his status for this week is hazy, at best. With No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (Achilles) missing the past two games, the 49ers acquired Keenan Allen at the trade deadline to provide additional depth. If Samuel is able to get back on the field against the Cowboys, he could find success against a defense that has given up 159.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, ninth-most i

Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Monangai has sat out the last four weeks with thumb and toe issues. The second-year ball carrier recording a 30-146-2 rushing line before his inactive streak makes it even more frustrating, so he'll hopefully get back to practice sooner rather than later. If he is healthy against Tampa Bay, he'll face a defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

Zay Flowers and the Ravens are at home to take on the Chargers in Week 10. He brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for another 17 yards during Baltimore's defeat in Week 9. Flowers and his fantasy managers are hoping the acquisition of Jacoby Brissett will provide a boost for the Ravens' passing game, as the former Cardinal will get his first Ravens start on Monday Night Football. Flowers does have a favorable matchup against a Chargers defense allowing 36.9 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs.

Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, Saquon was otherwise held in check with 54 scrimmage yards in a dismal 27-10 loss to Washington. Philadelphia does not appear likely to trade Barkley to a contender, leaving him primed for a revenge game against his former squad, the New York Giants, in Week 9. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.

Jake Ferguson left the last game for Dallas due to an ankle injury. His status remains up in the air for Week 9 versus Indianapolis. Ferguson has failed to register a single catch in each of the last two contests. Brevyn Spann-Ford could see additional looks if Ferguson is sidelined. Spann-Ford snagged five passes for 31 yards following Ferguson's departure. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

news.text: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.. Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

players.outlook: In Week 10, Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the winless Chargers to town. He caught both of his targets for 19 yards during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. Andrews actually led the team in receiving yardage and was second behind Zay Flowers and Justice Hill in receptions, who each recorded three. Jacoby Brissett will earn his first start for the Ravens after being acquired via trade, but Andrews could find it difficult to operate versus a Chargers defense allowing 10.0 fantasy points per game (3rd) to TEs.

Will Shipley found the end zone last game for the Eagles but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.

news.text: Shipley (foot) remained limited in practice Thursday.. Shipley is still on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened this week. With Saquon Barkley healthy right now, Shipley has minimal fantasy appeal in a broken Philadelphia offense that is near the bottom of the league in most categories over the last month.

players.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals welcome the Steelers to town for a Week 10 divisional clash. He caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns during Cincinnati's Week 9 victory. Higgins recorded two TDs for the second consecutive game, and he now has five receiving scores over his last three outings. He'll look to keep up the pace versus a Pittsburgh defense he cooked for a 6-90-1 line on seven targets in Week 3.

Travis Etienne (hamstring) will likely operate as New Orleans' top running back if active for the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Etienne has been sidelined for the Saints' last five games due to a hamstring issue, but his 21-day practice window is expected to be opened soon. If active for the Week 10 divisional matchup, Etienne is expected to thrive against a Panthers defense that's already allowed 12 touchdowns to opposing running backs in just eight games this year.

Jordan Love will look to keep his MVP campaign rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Love was on fire again in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three passing touchdowns and a 13-yard rushing score. Green Bay's signal caller has now dished out two or more touchdowns and passed for 270 or more yards in each of his last three outings. He'll rematch a Vikings defense that he threw for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against in a Week 1 loss.

Stroud spreads the ball around to a deep Texans WR room that also includes Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison and Kayshon Boutte. Collins has been targeted five or fewer times in each of the past three games, scoring just once over that span while averaging three catches for 45 yards. He'll need to pick up the pace to reach the 1,000-yard receiving mark for a fourth consecutive season. Kendre Miller is expected to operate as the Saints' top rusher in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. While Travis Etienne (hamstring) has been sidelined, Miller has averaged 11 carries per game, but just 28.8 rushing yards per game (2.6 yards per carry). Despite the lack of efficiency, Miller has led New Orleans' backfield in carries three consecutive games, which bodes well for his outlook while Etienne remains out. Miller could find success against the Browns' defense in Week 9, as they've given up 4.9 yards per carry to opposing running backs this season.

Over his last three contests, he strung together a 6-66-0 receiving line on nine targets to go along with his one-yard TD run, securing two receptions in each outing. In Week 10, Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Steelers in an AFC North showdown on Sunday Night Football. He caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a TD during Cincinnati's 34-17 win in Week 9. Chase led his team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, and he has now turned in two consecutive games with 10-plus catches, 140-plus yards, and a score. Chase will aim to keep rolling against a Pittsburgh defense he burned for a 9-98-1 line on 12 targets back in Week 3.

Roschon Johnson could return to being a depth option as the Bears play Tampa Bay in Week 9. Johnson has benefited from the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) during the last four weeks, as he's averaging 9.5 touches per game in this stretch. Unfortunately, Monangai could return in the upcoming home front, which would shrink Johnson's role. Even if Monangai sits out again, Johnson would be a tough play against a Bucs defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

Tank Dell looked like his old self in his second game back from a nearly two-year absence due to a knee injury. He caught four of nine targets for 105 yards and a TD in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers after securing a 43-yard catch against the Giants in Dell's Week 8 return to action. If Dell is still floating around on waivers in your league, he's worth adding in most formats, as he was a viable fantasy WR2 prior to his injury and just turned 27 years old. Jeremiyah Love has missed Arizona's past two games due to an ankle injury but could return in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love is slated to practice this week, though that doesn't guarantee that he'll suit up versus Dallas. If the rookie running back misses another game, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would likely continue to split the Cardinals' backfield work. Arizona's ground game could be set for a big day against a Dallas defense that is giving up 20.9 fantasy points per game to running backs, seventh-worst in the league.

news.text: Arizona placed Love (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.. Love's move to IR was fully expected, after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Tuesday that the rookie first-round pick was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain and was facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. While Love is on the mend, Tyler Allgeier is expected to step into a lead role out of the Arizona backfield beginning with the team's Week 9 game against Seattle.

players.outlook: Cam Little connected on a season-high four field goals in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens, bringing him up to 14-for-16 through eight games this season. He has attempted 10 more PATs than FGs behind Jacksonville's efficient offense, but Little should enjoy plenty of kicking opportunities in Week 10, as the Titans are surrendering 24.9 points per game while the Jaguars are scoring 28.6 points per game. Tennessee has allowed 17 successful field goals, which is tied for 10th most in the NFL, so Little is a set-and-forget fantasy starter for Week 10.

Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top pass catcher in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Olave added another productive outing to his impressive 2026 campaign during the Week 9 overtime win against the Browns, catching seven of 12 targets for 98 yards. On the season, Olave ranks sixth in the NFL in targets per game (10.4) and seventh in receiving yards per game (91.8). Olave's high volume will likely continue as well, with Tyler Shough tied for the most pass attempts per game (38.5) in the league through eight games. However, Skattebo pushed to play in the contest, and as a result looks primed to return to the starting lineup in Week 10 versus the Commanders. Washington has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026, though, allowing just 102.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the league. In addition, the Commanders have yielded just seven rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the NFL.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

Rhamondre Stevenson is uncertain to suit up for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury. New England fell into a big hole in Week 9, limiting Stevenson's carries prior to the injury, and he finished with a season-low six for the third time this season. His passing game involvement included a second touchdown reception in three weeks. If he plays, Stevenson figures to again lead the Patriots' backfield since TreVeyon Henderson will also likely be sidelined. Stevenson's rushing yard expectations can be tempered against a defense that's allowing a mere 3.9 yards per carry.

Malik Nabers had a four-game 100-yard receiving streak snapped last game for the Giants. Nabers had five catches for 43 yards in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. He was targeted eight times. He will look to rebound in Week 10 against a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.

Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. St. Brown led Detroit in all receiving categories against the Dolphins in Week 9, bringing in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards. The star wide receiver is on track for another dominant year, but he hasn't logged a touchdown since Week 3. He enters a favorable matchup versus a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. McMillan salvaged his fantasy day with a late score in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos, catching four of six targets for 56 yards. The Arizona product has cooled down since his monstrous performance in Week 4 (14-192-2), averaging 5.0 receptions and 60.0 receiving yards per game over his last four contests. Despite this, McMillan could find success against a Saints secondary that's allowed 31.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

Bo Nix put together another fourth-quarter comeback in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. While the third-year QB's own numbers are nothing special this season, he's led his team to a 6-2 record and first place in the AFC West. Week 8 was only the second time in eight games he's thrown for multiple touchdowns, and his 59.6% completion rate and 6.0 yards per attempt are both career lows. Nix could be poised for his best game of the season in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

Christian McCaffrey will seek to add to his seven-game scoring streak when San Francisco faces Dallas in Week 10. With two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) this past Sunday against Las Vegas, McCaffrey has gotten into the end zone at least once in each of his past seven games. While he has been logging fewer touches per game this season, McCaffrey continues to be a workhorse for the 49ers and has averaged 4.5 yards per rush, his highest mark since 2023. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. Dallas Goedert has caught at least four passes in four-straight games for the Eagles. He has amassed 28 targets over that span. Unfortunately, Goedert is averaging less than 45 yards receiving per contest during that time period. He has also been held out of the end zone. With backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Goedert's prospects may not be getting any better. In Week 9, the Eagles will face a Giants defense allowing just 184.9 passing yards per tilt, which us third in the NFL.

Tyler Warren has drawn at least seven targets in five of his last six appearances. The 2025 first-round pick remains a weekly fantasy starter at TE thanks to his hefty volume, even though he's averaging just 5.2 yards per target in the Colts' low-octane passing offense. Warren and the Colts will face a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed six receiving TDs in eight games to TEs. In addition to two touchdown catches, Warren has one rushing score this season.

Khalil Shakir remains an efficient secondary option in the Bills' passing game ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Jets. He caught four passes in Week 9, the fifth time in eight outings he's done so, resulting in 50 or more yards at the same rate. Shakir has only one touchdown, and the Jets' secondary has allowed just nine touchdown catches by receivers, likely limiting Shakir's potential in Week 10, but his role and usage are clear and steady, setting him up for stability as a potential streamer.

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

Stefon Diggs had a two-game scoring streak snapped last game for Washington. Diggs caught three passes for 51 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams. Diggs will look for a return to the end zone in Week 10 versus the Giants. New York has given up 14 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 20th in the league. However, do not expect much in the way of yardage, as the G-Men are yielding just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

Kenyon Sadiq's usage remains inconsistent ahead of the Jets' Week 10 matchup with the Bills. While Sadiq flashed with four catches in Week 9, he previously had only five grabs in his previous five games despite the Jets throwing more than 30 times in each outing. Sadiq remains high on potential but low on opportunity, suggesting a volatile ceiling/floor against a defense that's allowed only one opposing tight end to score.

DK Metcalf and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for a divisional clash in Week 10. He caught just one of six targets for four yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8, giving the 28-year-old a 3-60-0 receiving line on 12 targets over his last two contests. Metcalf and the Steelers didn't have to throw much while playing most of Week 8 with a double-digit advantage, but that could change in Week 10 versus a high-powered Bengals offense on Sunday Night Football. In his first matchup against Cincinnati, Metcalf corralled three of five targets for 31 yards and his only TD of the season.

Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Brooks is considered week-to-week after tweaking the same groin he first injured during training camp in the Week 2 win over the Falcons. Prior to his injury, the Texas product was clearly operating as Carolina's second RB, tallying just nine carries for 30 yards and two catches for 43 yards over the team's first two contests. news.text: Brooks (groin) remained a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.. Brooks is still on injured reserve but appears to be tracking toward a Week 11 return against Baltimore on Sunday. Chuba Hubbard should remain head-and-shoulders above Brooks on the depth chart as the clear RB1 for Carolina, but the Panthers likely also want to use the rest of the season to see if Brooks can stay healthy for a stretch and produce when given opportunities. Brooks is worth adding in fantasy, but his role will need to be defined before plugging him in lineups.

players.outlook: Daniel Jones is staying in Indianapolis after the trade deadline, though it's fair to wonder how long the 2-7 Colts will stick with the struggling veteran over younger options Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. Jones hasn't produced a multi-TD performance all season, and that drought seems unlikely to conclude in Week 10 against a Dolphins defense that has been better recently and just held Detroit's Jared Goff without a TD in Week 9. A.J. Brown will look to return from a two-week absence when the Patriots face the Lions in Week 10. Limited to just three games thus far, Brown amassed 16 targets in his last two outings and figures to again draw heavy volume if healthy. In a game where the Patriots could be down their top two running backs, a pass-heavy shootout appears possible, setting Brown up for a big game against a Lions secondary that's allowing 8.0 yards per target to opposing wideouts.

However, the veteran wideout sustained a hamstring injury while making a reception in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the loss, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is" once the team returns to the United States. In Week 9, he had nine carries for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for another 18 yards to help Cincinnati win a fourth straight game. Brown's production has been somewhat underwhelming from a fantasy perspective, as he's registered just one touchdown across eight outings in 2026. He'll look to find the end zone against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed just four TDs to the position and is coming off a bye.

Hunter Henry figures to be a popular option for the Patriots in Week 10 against a Lions defense that struggles against opposing tight ends. Henry has just three targets in each of his last two games and has topped 48 yards just twice all season, but Week 10 presents an inviting opportunity. Detroit has allowed 11 touchdown receptions to tight ends and 8.2 yards per target, the highest numbers across the league. With New England potentially missing its top two running backs, a pass-heavy script would set Henry up for top-end production.

Chig Okonkwo has been targeted at least six times in three of the last four contests for the Commanders. Okonkwo caught six passes for 57 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams last game. Okonkwo has at least 55 receiving yards in three of the last four games for Washington. However, he will face a difficult test in the form of the New York Giants in Week 10. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

Caleb Williams will look to stay solid as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Williams pieced together another solid outing in Chicago's Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown. The starting quarterback has now thrown for 860 yards and four touchdowns in his last three games, and he's passed for 240 or more yards in all but one outing this season. He'll shift focus to a Tampa Bay squad that's ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

Josh Allen will seek a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. In Week 9 at Minnesota, Allen, in the face of constant pressure, had his first game of the year with just one touchdown while being held under 250 yards for the fourth time. The Jets have allowed a 16:1 TD:INT ratio through nine games, but Allen threw for only 148 yards and no scores against them in his lone 2025 matchup, suggesting a lower-than-usual ceiling for arguably the league's best quarterback.

Matt Gay was afforded few opportunities in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, connecting on a 50-yard attempt for his only field goal and converting both his PATs. The veteran kicker has a 90.5% FG success rate on the season, going 19-for-21, and he has yet to miss an extra point in 2026, but his erratic weekly volume limits his fantasy utility. Gay isn't likely to see much volume in Week 10 against a Seahawks team allowing 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth in the league.

news.text: Gay (hip) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.. Gay made both of his two field-goal tries and his only extra-point attempt during Sunday's 21-13 loss versus the Seahawks, but it looks like he might have picked up a hip injury at some point along the way. As long as he can manage a full practice Thursday or Friday, he should still be in a good position to suit up in Week 11 against the Broncos.

players.outlook: Harrison Mevis' job may be on the line heading into the Rams' Week 6 contest against the Cardinals. Mevis missed both of his field-goal attempts in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, including a 50-yarder in the first quarter and a blocked 48-yarder in overtime that could have won the game. He's now just 5-for-9 on FG tries this season, including 3-for-6 from 40-to-49 yards out. Should Mevis still be kicking for the Rams in Week 6, he may be limited mostly to extra points versus a Cardinals defense that has yielded 18 PAT tries to just six FG attempts this season.

Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns welcome the Texans to town for a Week 10 AFC clash. He caught both of his targets for 42 yards, including an impressive 39-yard touchdown in overtime, during Cleveland's 23-22 OT loss in Week 9. Fannin was quiet until the extra frame, a disappointing development after he erupted for a 10-154-0 line on 12 targets in his previous outing. He'll look to stay hot despite a difficult matchup versus Houston's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (10.1) to TEs.

C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD masterpiece in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers and has thrown 10 touchdown passes over the past three games. He has showcased an elite ceiling with four games north of 300 passing yards this season, so the surging Stroud is a start-worthy Week 10 option, even in a road game against a Browns defense that ranks among the 10 stingiest units against the pass. The Ohio State product is no stranger to playing in the Buckeye State this time of year, though it's worth noting that the Browns are 3-0 at home while allowing just 17.3 points per game at

J.K. Dobbins may have lost his hold on the top job in the Broncos' backfield. In a Week 8 comeback win over Kansas City, it was rookie Jonah Coleman who got the biggest workload and who scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run. Dobbins recorded just seven carries, his second straight game getting single-digit touches, and his woeful 3.3 yards per carry doesn't make a strong case for a bigger role. With RJ Harvey on injured reserve, Dobbins should retain the No. 2 job for the next few weeks. The veteran might be able to make a splash on limited carries in Week 9 against a Panthers defens

Rome Odunze figures to be a top option in Chicago's passing game again as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Odunze finished Week 8 with his second-highest yardage of the season, bringing in four of six targets for 87 yards. The third-year wide receiver has eight catches for 156 yards in the last two weeks, which is his most productive two-game stretch so far this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

Jakobi Meyers is a strong Week 10 flex play against a Titans defense that has struggled to cover wide receivers. Tennessee is allowing a league-high 15.3 catches for 195 yards per game to the position. Meyers has had an up-and-down season as Jacksonville's No. 2 WR but has trended in the right direction recently, notching two of his three best performances this season for both receiving yards and targets within the last three games. He's more likely to produce a peak than a valley in the first of Jacksonville's two meetings this season against Tennessee's league-worst secondary.

news.text: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.. Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

players.outlook: In Week 10, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers visit their divisional-rival Bengals on Sunday Night Football. He rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown while catching one of two targets for no gain during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 9. Warren matched his career high for rushing yards and produced his third 100-plus-yard effort in his last four games. In Week 3, he generated 176 scrimmage yards on 20 touches in his first matchup against Cincinnati, so he'll be hungry to put up similar numbers on the road.

James Cook's high volume creates a high floor and ceiling heading into the Bills' Week 10 matchup with the Jets. Cook amassed a season-high 31 carries in Week 9, his sixth game in eight outings with 20-plus touches, and has topped 100 total yards at the same ratio while scoring in seven straight games. While the Bills have a short week coming off a Monday night game, nothing has been shown to suggest Cook's role will be reduced. Justin Jefferson will hope to see better play at the QB position in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Jefferson reeled in just three of his whopping 11 targets for 58 yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. The all-out struggles of Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), were fully seen in Jefferson's receiving line, but the trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins re-united him with the QB he's had the most success with. Garrett Wilson needs to clear the concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Bills in Week 10. Wilson has seen sporadic usage when healthy, amassing double-digit targets three times while averaging 5.8 looks in five additional outings. Assuming he receives a clean bill of health, he'll face a secondary that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts. With the Jets likely falling into an early hole, a pass-heavy game flow is probable, with Wilson being an active participant.

Jordyn Tyson's role in the Saints' offense is expected to continue growing during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Tyson was sidelined for New Orleans' first seven games this season due to a hamstring. He was relatively underwhelming in his NFL debut, catching four of five targets for 30 yards while also losing a fumble in the Week 9 overtime win over the Browns. Despite this, Tyler Shough is tied for the league-lead in pass attempts per game (38.5) and Tyson is expected to get more involved in the Saints' offense as the season continues, so his fantasy outlook remains positive. Friday's practice report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

players.outlook: Chad Ryland's opportunities could be influenced by a new Cardinals' starting quarterback (Carson Beck) against the Rams in Week 10. Arizona is coming off a battle against a top defensive unit, and Ryland got just one chance to kick -- making a short field goal -- in Week 9 against Seattle. Gardner Minshew suffered an elbow injury in that contest, leading the rookie Beck to presumably make his NFL debut as the starting QB against the Rams. Perhaps Ryland will get multiple field-goal opportunities against a Los Angeles defense that has allowed the most FG tries (26) in the NFL this season.

Kyren Williams may be asked to log a heftier workload than usual for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Williams rushed for just 45 yards -- his second-lowest mark of the season -- on 15 carries against Washington in Week 9, adding 16 yards on three catches. However, Los Angeles is going to be without wideout Puka Nacua (knee) for multiple weeks, and with Davante Adams (hamstring) still on IR, the team may turn more to its ground game  -- led by Williams and Blake Corum -- to carry the load. Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. players.outlook: Ladd McConkey didn't log any snaps in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, as back spasms during pregame workouts kept him on the sideline. The third-year wide receiver has seen a full workload in just two of the seven games he's been active for, and with the team winless on the season, there's little incentive for the Chargers to take any risks with his health. McConkey has been productive when he's been in the lineup, but it's becoming harder to predict when that will be. If he manages to play in Week 10, he'll be facing a Ravens secondary that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game

news.text: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.. McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, was also limited Wednesday. Per  Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

players.outlook: Colston Loveland will look to remain a high-volume option as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Loveland was solid again in a Week 8 win over the Bears, bringing in seven of nine targets for 65 yards but losing a fumble. The second-year tight end has now brought in six or more receptions in four of his last five games, and he's found the end zone in two of his last three. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 22nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

news.text: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.. Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

players.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 10 road game against the Browns, but he has just 46 receiving yards over that span and is averaging a meager 36 receiving yards per game this season. He has maintained a prominent role in a high-ceiling Houston passing offense, drawing at least five targets in all but one game, but Hutchinson hasn't done much with those opportunities and had just three career TDs in 3.5 seasons prior to his current two-game scoring streak. Isaiah Likely found the end zone again for the Giants last game. Likely snagged five passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in the 19-11 win over Philadelphia. Likely now has scored four touchdowns in his last four contests. He is a great bet to find the end zone again versus a suspect Washington pass defense. Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns this season, which is tied for 25th in the league.  In addition, the Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league.

D'Andre Swift will look to build on a high-volume performance as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Swift was, for the most part, stymied by a tough Seattle front in Week 8, averaging just 2.6 yards per carry, but he still put together a monster game with three touchdowns and 69 yards off a season-high 27 rushes. The veteran has directly benefited from the absence of position mate Kyle Monangai in the last four weeks, which can especially be seen through his seven touchdowns in that stretch. Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

news.text: Doubs (shoulder) is hopeful to return after the Patriots' Week 11 bye and isn't expected to face a long-term absence, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.. With Doubs already on injured reserve, this report offers a more encouraging timeline after Sunday's shoulder injury. He'll still need to miss at least four games, but a possible return after the bye would keep the Patriots from being without one of their key wide receivers for an extended stretch. Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be in line for increased snaps alongside A.J. Brown and slot man DeMario Douglas with Doubs sidelined.

players.outlook: DeMario Douglas will look to continue his recent surge when the Patriots face the Lions in Week 10. Douglas had a season-high 102 yards on nine targets in Week 9, a game that developed into a pass-heavy shootout. A similar game script could be on tap against a Detroit defense that has allowed the fourth-most passing yards. A potential return for A.J. Brown may reduce Douglas' targets, but with the expectation the Patriots will throw often, he can post 65 yards or better for the sixth time in seven weeks.

Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. players.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Robinson was one of Atlanta's few bright spots during the Week 9 loss to the Bengals, accumulating 147 yards and a touchdown on 25 touches. The Texas product is currently averaging the third-most touches per game (22.2) in the NFL, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs despite a tough matchup. Kansas City's defense has given up just 20.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through eight games this year.

news.text: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.. The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

players.outlook: Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

Tony Pollard delivered consecutive elite performances prior to Tennessee's Week 9 bye, racking up 292 scrimmage yards and five TDs across losses to the Browns and Bengals. Prior to that two-game stretch, he had just one TD through seven games and no 100-yard performances. If he isn't traded prior to Tuesday's deadline, Pollard would maintain fantasy RB2 upside for Week 10 despite a difficult matchup against a Jaguars defense that's holding RBs to 68 yards per game. Even before his recent uptick in production, Pollard had a solid floor as the clear lead back for Tennessee.
