Even with Brock Bowers ahead of him on the depth chart, Mayer's role is large enough to give him some value heading into a Week 10 clash with a Seahawks defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Dalton Schultz is a borderline fantasy starter at TE for Week 10 against the Browns. He ranks ninth among TEs with 46 receiving yards per game but has yet to score this season and has a meager five TDs in 42 regular-season appearances since the start of the 2024 season. Cleveland has allowed five TDs to the position in nine games, as well as 58 yards per game.

Quentin Johnston caught his first touchdown of the season in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, but it was also his only catch of the contest on four targets. The fourth-year wide receiver has hauled in more than two passes just twice in seven appearances this season, scratching out a 13-260-1 line on 30 targets. He's generally failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey's frequent absences in one of the NFL's most dysfunctional offenses. Johnston is unlikely to suddenly break out in Week 10, even against a Ravens secondary that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the Steelers for an AFC North clash in Week 10. He corralled both of his targets for 11 yards during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Gesicki's five-game streak with a touchdown came to an end with all three of Joe Burrow's TD passes going to Ja'Marr Chase (one) and Tee Higgins (two). Gesicki's fantasy value has been reliant on TDs in 2026, so he'll try to start another streak of consecutive trips to the endzone versus a Pittsburgh defense his initial scoring stretch started against back in Week 3.

Darius Cooper finished second on the Eagles in targets last game behind Makai Lemon. With starting wideouts DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks both sidelined due to injury, Cooper saw an increase in looks. Unfortunately, Cooper could only manage two catches for 19 yards in the dismal 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Cooper has just 11 catches on the season. In Week 9, the Eagles will face a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 189.4 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

Calvin Ridley (hip) sat out for the Titans in Week 7 against the Browns. Even if he returns for Week 8 against the Bengals, Ridley won't be a viable fantasy option. He has caught a pass in only three of six appearances this season, with season totals of five catches for 81 yards while operating in a depth role at WR.

Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Johnson saw little volume but saved his fantasy day with a score in Week 9, catching two of three targets for 34 yards and a touchdown. He's been relatively underwhelming over the last three contests, catching just three of seven targets for 41 yards and a touchdown. This is especially concerning due to the return of 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson, who will likely take more receiving volume away from Johnson as the season progresses. However, Johnson could thrive agains

AJ Barner will look to build upon his two-touchdown game when Seattle visits Las Vegas in Week 10. Barner had one score through the air and another on the ground in a Week 9 win over Arizona.  Though his receiving output has remained modest, Barner has been getting more opportunities to carry the ball in short-yardage situations in recent weeks, as he's logged six carries over his past three games. He'll seek to get into the end zone against the Raiders, who have given up the second-most TDs (eight) to tight ends this season.

Travis Hunter has just one fantasy-relevant performance on offense this season while playing much more cornerback than wide receiver for the Jaguars. The 2025 second overall pick has the talent to thrive if injuries and/or roster moves open up more opportunities on offense, but Hunter can't be trusted as a starter outside of individual defensive player formats as things stand. Expect Hunter to play just a few snaps on offense as usual in Week 10, which won't give him many chances to capitalize on facing Tennessee's generous secondary.

In Week 10, Rashod Bateman and the Ravens host a Chargers defense allowing 36.9 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs. He caught one of two targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. Bateman now has one or fewer receptions in three of his last four outings, tallying a 4-55-0 line on 10 targets over that stretch. He'll have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting under center, but Bateman should be left on fantasy benches until proven otherwise.

Dontayvion Wicks missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky ankle. In fact, Wicks has missed the last two contests because of the ailment.  If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.

news.text: Wicks (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.. Wicks is seeking his first game action since Week 6 due to an ankle injury, and he still has some work to do after kicking off Week 11 prep with back-to-back capped sessions. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to play Sunday versus the Steelers.

players.outlook: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

news.text: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.. While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly afte

players.outlook: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

news.text: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.. This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

players.outlook: Tyler Higbee may need to ramp up his production for the Rams' passing game to be successful, beginning with a Week 10 matchup in Arizona. Higbee continued his recent trend of limited production this past Sunday against Washington, logging just one catch for 13 yards on five targets. He's recorded two or fewer receptions in three straight games, but Los Angeles may need Higbee to be more impactful after losing star WR Puka Nacua for what is likely to be multiple weeks due to a knee injury. The Cardinals rank 27th in the NFL with 10.4 fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends this season.

Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching d

news.text: Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver is "100 percent healthy" and fully recovered from his November 2024 right knee surgery and plans to work out for interested teams once he's released by the 49ers, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.. After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco s

players.outlook: Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns

news.text: McLaurin (knee) underwent surgery Friday to repair the torn patellar tendon in his left knee, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.. The surgery was conducted in New York, and McLaurin has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. His availability for the start of the 2027 campaign will also be in question, as the veteran wideout faces a lengthy rehab process. The Commanders will move forward with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks atop the wideout depth chart this season.

players.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the 3-5 Texans in Week 10. He caught two of four targets for 37 yards during Week 9's overtime loss to the Saints. Through nine contests this season, Jeudy has amassed a modest 18-208-0 line on 28 targets. He remains off the fantasy radar despite a favorable matchup versus a Houston defense allowing 38.5 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs, which ranks 30th.

Treylon Burks did not play last game for the Commanders due to a foot injury. In his place, Van Jefferson was the surprise leading receiver, snagging a team-high 58 yards and a touchdown in the 20-13 loss to Washington. Even if Burks can return in Week 10, he will face a difficult test in the form of the New York Giants. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

news.text: Rams head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday during his appearance on the "Coach McVay Show" that he remains optimistic Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) will return from injured reserve this season, though he was unwilling to guarantee that the tight end will be activated by the time his 21-day evaluation window closes, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. "I'm reluctant to get too far ahead of anything, just because -- but yes, that is something we'd want to avoid if he's not prepared," McVay said, regarding the possibility of Ferguson being shut down.. After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sund

players.outlook: Rashid Shaheed (knee) has missed Seattle's past two games and isn't certain to return in Week 10 against the Raiders. Shaheed hasn't practiced since getting hurt in Week 7, and he'll likely need to return to at least a few limited sessions before being ready to play in games again. Should Shaheed sit out another contest, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton will likely continue to be the Seahawks' top wideouts behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If Shaheed can suit up, though, he'll face a Raiders defense that has allowed 27 passing plays of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

Keon Coleman continues to struggle for meaningful action as the Bills prepare to face the Jets in Week 10. Coleman drew six targets in Week 9, the second time he's done so in three games, but finished with only 17 yards, the fourth time he's been limited to under 20 yards. With DJ Moore healthy, Coleman is at best the third option in Buffalo's passing game, and facing a defense that's allowed just nine touchdown receptions to wideouts in as many outings doesn't give Coleman much of a ceiling.

Cooper Kupp continues to be quiet this season ahead of Seattle's Week 10 visit to Las Vegas. Kupp logged a 3-32-0 receiving line this past Sunday against Arizona despite Rashid Shaheed (knee) continuing to be sidelined. Kupp's four targets in the game were actually his third-most through nine games, emphasizing how little attention he's gotten from the Seahawks' quarterbacks this season. With that said, he at least has a good matchup coming up, as the Raiders have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season -- tied for second-most in the NFL.

Brian Thomas has been almost completely phased out of Jacksonville's offense, with just one catch over the past four games. Even a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Titans defense that is allowing the most catches and yards per game to WRs won't be enough to get Thomas back on the fantasy radar.

Roman Wilson and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He failed to catch his only target prior to exiting Pittsburgh's 34-22 win in Week 5 with a finger injury. Wilson has already been ruled out for the trip to Tampa Bay, meaning Germie Bernard should see a boost in playing time and opportunities in his absence.

news.text: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.. With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over th

players.outlook: Konata Mumpfield may need to step up for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Mumpfield has been quiet of late, logging no more than two catches and 20 yards over his past six games. However, with Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR and Puka Nacua (knee) expected to join him there, Los Angeles is likely going to need some of its other wideouts to start being more productive. Mumpfield has a good matchup against Arizona, as the Cardinals have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts, tied for second-most in the NFL.

Jayden Reed will remain inactive as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

news.text: The Packers officially placed Reed (neck) on injured reserve Wednesday.. Coach Matt LaFleur announced earlier Wednesday that Reed required surgery on his neck injury that'll be season-ending, so this transaction was inevitable. Reed has been contained to just nine regular-season appearances the last two years due to health concerns, but LaFleur did relay to Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that he doesn't believe the current issue will threaten the wide receiver's career. With Reed sidelined for the rest of the campaign, Skyy Moore will operate as Green Bay's No. 3 WR behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

players.outlook: Malik Washington's workload appears to be drying up ahead of the Dolphins' Week 10 matchup with the Colts. Washington averaged 7.2 targets in five games prior to Miami's Week 6 bye but has just 12 looks over the three games since, reaching 28 yards just once. Indianapolis is allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but with Miami's passing game struggling and Caleb Douglas emerging, Washington's decreasing role will make for a risky play with minimal upside.

Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens are at home to square off against the winless Chargers in Week 10. The rookie wideout was not targeted during Baltimore's 33-10 loss in Week 9, as the team attempted just 19 total passes. Lane is still firmly behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman on the WR pecking order, but the Ravens are hoping the acquisition of Jacoby Brissett will provide a boost for the passing game overall. Still, Lane should remain on fantasy waiver wires until we know more about this offense.

Elic Ayomanor didn't capitalize on Carnell Tate's (shoulder) absence in Week 8 against the Bengals. Tate is likely to return in Week 10 against the Jaguars, pushing Ayomanor back to third in Tennessee's wide-receiver pecking order. Ayomanor hasn't scored since Week 1 and is averaging just 26 yards per game. Even against a Jaguars defense that gives up most of its yards through the air, Ayomanor doesn't profile as a viable Week 10 fantasy option.

Kalif Raymond remains a secondary option in Chicago's offense heading into Week 9 against Tampa Bay. Raymond finished a Week 8 win over the Seahawks with two catches for 14 yards, and he tacked on one rush for 39 yards. The veteran has taken a major backseat to Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the WR hierarchy at this point in the season, but he's still a reliable option when needed for quarterback Caleb Williams. Raymond will face a Bucs defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

Gavin Bartholomew will aim to stay involved as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Even with T.J. Hockenson healthy in Week 7 against the Colts, Bartholomew got a target and brought it in for 17 yards. The rookie tight end has been a solid secondary option in the passing game, with seven catches for 54 yards across his first six games. He'll face a Detroit defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to TEs.

Jake Bates will look to benefit from high volume again as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Bates was perfect in a Week 9 win over Miami, nailing five total kicks which included four field goals. The third-year boot has now made multiple field goals for the third straight game, with Detroit's offense cooling down slightly after a crazy start to the year. New England has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers so far this campaign.

Oronde Gadsden was held in check in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, catching two of three targets for 17 yards. The second-year tight end has struggled to fit into offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and this season he has as many games with zero catches as he does with performances of more than three grabs. Overall, Gadsden has managed a 19-172-1 line on 29 targets over eight contests. He'll look to make a difference in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Eli Raridon is trending favorably ahead of the Patriots' Week 10 matchup against a Lions defense that struggles against tight ends. Raridon has collected at least four targets in three straight games, even with fellow tight end Hunter Henry healthy, and the Lions are allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. While still a secondary option in New England's passing game, Raridon can garner enough attention to be a viable option in a plus matchup.

Ka'imi Fairbairn has made multiple field goals in five consecutive games, going 14-for-14 over that productive stretch. Houston's standout kicker remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter for a Week 10 road game against the Browns, who are allowing 21.8 points per game. Cleveland has allowed 19 made field goals in nine games, while Fairbairn has missed just once on 19 attempts through eight games while making all 21 of his PAT tries.

Cairo Santos will look to build on a solid showing as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Santos made all of his kicks in Chicago's Week 8 win over the Seahawks, nailing two field goal attempts and four XPAs. The veteran kicker had also missed a field goal in three straight games before this matchup, so he's hopefully now back on track. Tampa Bay has ranked 13th in fantasy points allowed to kickers so far this campaign.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

Noah Gray logged just one target in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, his lowest volume since Week 2, but he caught it for an 11-yard gain. The backup tight end has produced a 15-184-1 line on 17 targets through eight games, and his already limited ceiling could shrink further if Patrick Mahomes misses time due to an elbow injury he picked up against the Jets. Regardless of who's under center, Gray will take on a Falcons defense in Week 10 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

Zach Ertz caught two passes last game for the Eagles, as he continues to fill in for his injured former understudy, Dallas Goedert. It appears that Goedert is unlikely to suit up in  Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. Ertz had four targets last game and could prove a useful safety valve with an otherwise young, inexperienced pass-catching corps. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 10 AFC North showdown against the Bengals. In Week 8, he went 2-for-3 on field goal attempts and connected on all three of his PATs to help Pittsburgh win its fourth straight game. Boswell misfired on a 57-yarder to end their first offensive possession, as the 35-year-old is now 4-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards out in 2026. However, he's had three or more FGAs in three consecutive outings, a trend that is likely to continue versus a Cincinnati team scoring the second-most points per game (30.0).

Jason Sanders brings a high ceiling into the Jets' Week 10 game against the Bills. He has attempted at least four field goals in consecutive games and three of his last four, with the Jets' offense failing to convert drives into touchdowns, evident by just six PATs over this four-game stretch. Buffalo is allowing the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing kickers, and field goals aren't likely to help the Jets in Week 10, but Sanders' recent run of scoring puts him in the streaming mix.

Cameron Dicker continues to benefit from the Chargers' inability to finish drives. The 26-year-old kicker has booted multiple field goals in five of the last six games, going 15-for-16 on FG attempts over that stretch but attempting just six extra points, converting them all. The steady volume gives Dicker a solid floor heading into a Week 10 clash with a Ravens team allowing 26.2 points per game, tied for 25th in the league.

So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

David Njoku led the Chargers' tight end group in receiving during a season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. That far overshadowed Oronde Gadsden's two catches for 32 yards, while Charlie Kolar was predictably limited to blocking duties in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Top wideout Ladd McConkey did get knocked out of the game with a rib injury, however, and if he misses additional time, there could be more looks available for Njoku. He gets a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that finished third in PPR

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

Cole Kmet will remain inactive as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury at the end of Chicago's Week 7 win over the Patriots. He's now been placed on IR and will officially sit out for the rest of the year. Kmet's absence should continue to give rookie tight end Sam Roush an uptick in usage.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

Greg Dulcich will again have a favorable matchup when the Dolphins face the Colts in Week 10. He was presented with the best possible matchup in Week 9 against Detroit but managed only 14 yards on four targets and remains without a touchdown reception on the season as Malik Willis struggled under center before being placed on the IR. Indianapolis has allowed seven touchdowns to tight ends, including one in each of their last three games, but Dulcich has been held to 43 yards or fewer in six of eight outings and now has to develop a rapport with new QB Kyle McCord. Dulcich is out of the Week 10

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

Evan McPherson and the Bengals battle the Steelers for an AFC North showdown in Week 10. He went 2-for-2 on field goals and made all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. McPherson is one of two kickers who are still perfect at this point in the season, and he'll look to keep that going versus a Pittsburgh defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for the fourth fewest.

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

Dominic Zvada rebounded last game for the Giants with four field goals. Zvada did not miss a boot, connecting from at least 48 yards on three of his four field goal tries. He also added an extra points in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. He should have plenty more opportunities to score in Week 10 versus a lackluster Washington squad. The Commanders are allowing 25.3 points per game, which is 24th in the NFL.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

Tommy Tremble is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top tight ends during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Despite having one of his best performances of the season in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos (4-24-1), Tremble was out-shined by Darren Waller, who caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a score. On the season, Tremble ranks second amongst Panthers tight ends in receptions (21), targets (29), yards (179) and touchdowns (three). However, Tremble is in for a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Saints defense that's allwed 65.1 receiving yards per game to opposing TEs thi

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

Colby Parkinson could be a big part of the Rams' passing game in Week 10 against Arizona. Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles with four catches against Washington this past Sunday, though he gained just 13 yards on those receptions. Still, the Rams are going to need some pass catchers to step up in the wake of a knee injury that is likely going to cause star wideout Puka Nacua to miss multiple games, and Parkinson has tallied at least four catches in each of the last three games in which he's played. Evan Engram failed to catch a pass in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, as his role as a receiver continues to dwindle. The veteran tight end has been targeted multiple times in seven of eight games so far in 2026, but that steady volume has resulted in just a 13-136-1 line on 25 targets. The potential return of possession receiver Pat Bryant from an ankle injury would also cut into Engram's limited usage. He'll try to make a splash in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator and that is tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Cade Otton is expected to serve as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has caught just one pass over Tampa Bay's last three games, making him hard to trust going forward. Since Baker Mayfield returned from injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, the Buccaneers have attempted just 14 passes, making it hard for their pass catchers to contribute to fantasy teams. Gunnar Helm capitalized on a favorable matchup when Tennessee met the Bengals in Week 8, setting career highs with five catches for 76 yards on nine targets.
